messages:
anya: Quick sync — I pushed a first-pass PRD for the Dedicated Capacity launch to the drive. Need alignment on SLA targets, throughput sizing heuristics, and autoscale requirements before we freeze scope. tl;dr: customer asks + enterprise sales wants predictable p95 latency and a clear burst policy.

jason: thanks, anya. can you paste the core SLA numbers here? easier to react inline.

anya: sure — from the doc: p99 uptime 99.9% SLA window, p95 latency target <= 220ms for seq=256 on a single A100-equivalent slot, sustained throughput per reserved GPU = ~14 seq/s for gpt-3.5–style model (quantized). burst multiplier x2 for up to 5 minutes, then queue/steal to fallback pool.

liam: question — how are we defining the latency measurement? tail across customer tokens or per-request end-to-end? need to be precise for SLO alerts.

anya: good point. doc says: end-to-end server-side token generation latency measured at the model gateway (post-auth, pre-response). we include batching overhead. will call it "gateway p95" in the PRD. open to wording.

eva: engineering note — the 220ms p95 for seq=256 is aggressive on older infra. we can hit it on newer cards + tuned kernels, but need to pair with a quantization profile and aggressive KV cache. otherwise cost jumps.

maya: customers also asked for predictable bursting during morning traffic spikes. they'd rather have short-term guaranteed bursts than opaque throttling.

jason: prioritization: if we must trade, keep uptime and predictable burst behavior above absolute latency target. customers accept slightly higher p95 if we guarantee service and no opaque failures.

liam: autoscale triggers proposal: CPU/GPU util > 75% & queue length > 10 requests for 30s -> scale up by 1 slot. scale down when util < 35% and queue == 0 for 180s. also sticky cooldown of 5m to avoid flip-flop. thoughts?

eva: yep that looks sensible. add a policy: if scale-up fails 3x in a 10m window, start graceful fallback flow to hosted pool and alert SRE.

ops-bot: deploy note — can create canary with 10% of reserved capacity routed to new autoscale policy. reply `yes` to create.

anya: acceptance criteria (first cut):
```
- Feature toggle enabled in prod for dedicated customers.
- SLA: p95 gateway latency <= 220ms for seq=256 on supported hardware (measured across last 24h).
- Availability: 99.9% measured monthly for dedicated pools.
- Burst: allow x2 capacity for up to 5 minutes, with documented escalation path.
- Autoscale: configured triggers + cooldowns implemented + rollback policy.
- Fallback: automatic routing to hosted variant within 30s on capacity failure.
- Regression tests + perf bench showing expected throughput per GPU.
```

maya: edge cases we must call out for customers: noisy neighbors on co-located tenants (if any), long-context sessions with KV cache eviction, and per-customer model pinning mismatch during rollout.

jason: suggest we add an explicit launch gate: run 3 customer pilots (staging->prod) for 2 weeks each with error budgets observed. if any pilot exceeds 0.1% unrecoverable failures, pause rollout.

liam: logging/observability ask: per-request trace id propagation, token-level cost breakdown, and a 1s-resolution rolling histogram for latency to debug spikes. Also export autoscale events to event store.

eva: runtime items: we'll need quantization profile defaults + a recommended config for batching (max_batch=64, batch_timeout=8ms) in the PRD. include a note on how to override per-tenant.

anya: agreed — I'll add those to the doc. can folks review the acceptance criteria and autoscale triggers by EOD? want to freeze PRD for scoping meeting tomorrow.

jason: I can take autoscale wording and the launch gate language.

liam: I'll add SRE runbook snippets + failure scenarios.

eva: I'll draft the recommended runtime config and perf numbers.

maya: i'll rope in 2 pilot customers and share contact windows.

ops-bot: reminder scheduled: PRD freeze meeting on calendar tomorrow 11:00am PT. :bell:

anya: thanks team — will update doc and ping when I push changes. :thumbsup:
